statement.p: Calculate \int_C \left(3 (x^2-y)\vec i + 4(y^2+x)\vec j\right) \cdot d\vec r if:
(a) C is the circle (x-5)^2+(y-5)^2=9 oriented counterclockwise.
(b) C is the circle (x-a)^2+(y-b)^2=R^2 in the xy-plane oriented counterclockwise.

static.solution:
(a) The curve, C, is closed and oriented in the correct direction for Green's Theorem. Writing A for the interior of the circle, we have \int_C \left( 3(x^2-y)\vec i +4(y^2+x)\vec j\right)\cdot d\vec r = \int_A \left(\frac{\partial}{\partial x}4 (y^2+x) - \frac{\partial}{\partial y}3(x^2-y)\right) dx\,dy = \int_A (4-(-3))\, dx\,dy = 7 \int_A dx\,dy = 7\cdot \mbox{Area of }A = 63\pi.
(b) The circle given has radius R and center (a,b). The argument in part (a) works for any circle of radius R, oriented counterclockwise. So the line integral has the value 7\pi R^2.
